summary: The root حثث (Hthth) primarily means to urge, incite, or encourage someone to do something. It implies a strong and often repeated prompting or instigation, pushing one towards an action or goal.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: حَثَّهُ حث حثه حثة, aor. حَثُثَ, inf. n. حَثٌّ, He hastened him, or hurried him uninterruptedly, or in any manner. (TA.) And حَثَّهُ عَلَيْهِ, (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. حَثُثَ, (Msb,) inf. n. حَثٌّ, (S, Msb, K,) with which are syn. [app. a quasi-inf. n.] and [an intensive inf. n.]; and; and, (S, K,) inf. n. تَحْثِيتٌ; (S;) and; (A, K;) and; (K;) and; (S, A, K;) He incited, excited, urged, or instigated, him to it, or to do it, (S, A, Msb, K,) namely, a thing; (S, Msb;) syn.

تحاثّوا أحاث تحاثوا, (S, A,) inf. n. تَحَاثٌّ, (K,) They incited, excited, urged, or instigated, one another. (K, TA.) You say, لَا يَتَحَاثَّونَ عَلَى طَعَامِ المِسْكيِنِ They do not incite, excite, urge, or instigate, one another to feed the needy. (S, TA.) And التَّقْوَى أَصْلُ مَا تَحَاثُّ النَّاسُ عَلَيْهِ [ Piety is the principal, or best, thing to which men incite one another. ] (A, TA.)
احتثّ احتث أحتث ٱحتث He was, or became, incited, excited, urged, or instigated. (S, K.) See also 1. This verb is both trans. and intrans. (K.)

R. Q. 1 حَثْحَثَ حثحث: see 1, in two places. Also He moved about [a thing]; or put [it] in motion, or into a state of commotion; (K;) [and so, as is implied in the M, voce فَدَّ, where it is used as meaning it (a bird) moved, or flapped, its wings.] You say, حَثْحَثَ المِيلَ فِى العَيْنِ He moved about the collyrium-style in the eye. (A, TA.) And [hence,] حَثْحَثُوا ٰلِكَ الأَمْرَ ثُمَّ تَرَكُوهُ (assumed tropical:) They stirred up ( حَرَّكُوا ) that affair, and then left it, or abandoned it.

حُثٌّ حث Small particles of straw. (S, K, TA.) Anything bruised, brayed, or broken into small particles. (L.) Coarse sand: (As, S:) or what is مُتَرَقْرِق, (K,) probably, [says SM,] a mistake for مَدْقُوق [ broken into small particles ], agreeably with an explanation of حُثٌّ in the L, for, as to مترقرق, [he adds,] I have not found it in any book, (TA, [meaning that he had not found a signification assigned to it that is appropriate here,]) of sand, and of earth, or dust: or what is dry, or…

حَثَاثٌ حثاث and Sleep; as also and. (TA.) You say, مَا ُقْتُ حثاثًا I tasted not sleep. (TA.) And مَا ٱكْتَحَلْتُ حَثَاثًا and حِثَاثًا I slept not: (S, K:) As says the latter; but A 'Obeyd asserts the former to be the more correct: (S:) Th mentions both. (TA.) And مَا كَحَلْتُ عَيْنِى بِحثاثٍ I have not anointed my eye with sleep. (TA.) And مَا جَعَلْتُ فِى عَيْنِى حثاثًا [ I have not put any sleep into my eye ]; (A, TA;) meaning I have been very wakeful.
حِثَاثٌ حثاث: see the next preceding paragraph.
حَثُوثٌ حثوث: see what next follows, in two places.

حَثِيثٌ حثيث, in the sense of حَاثَّةٌ, A woman inciting, exciting, urging, or instigating. (TA.) And in the sense of مَحْثُوثَةٌ, A woman incited, excited, urged, or instigated. (TA.) [So, too, a man.] And [hence,] A sharp man, quick in his affair; as though his soul incited him; as also. (TA.) And Quick, or swift; as also and and: (K:) pl. of the first حِثَاثٌ. (L.) You say فَرَسٌ حَثِيثُ السَّيْرِ [ A horse quick, or swift, of pace ].
حِثِّيثَى حثيث حثيثى حثيثي حثيثيي: see 1.
حَثْحَاثٌ حثحاث: see حَثَاثٌ: and see also حَثِيثٌ, in four places.
حُثْحُوثٌ حثحوث: see 1: and see also حَثَاثٌ: and حَثِيثٌ.
فَرَسٌ جَوَادُ المَحَثَّةِ فرس جواد المحثه فرس جواد المحثة A horse that runs repeatedly when incited [ to do so ]. (S.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
